answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to forge a stake-backed bond before it may trade: the agent locks tokens that are slashed if it misbehaves, so creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand bonds. Like ore locked in ferrous rock on a high mesa, the deposit is hard to reach and harder to duplicate cheaply - an attacker must pay real capital per identity, while honest agents keep their bond and earn fees. The cost scales with the attack, not with the honest network.
